metadata.case_name: LEE WAI KIN v. CHENG HON KIT JACKER

plaintiff.occupation_before: Sales manager of a trading company responsible for promoting the sale of Chinese medicine in the South China region including Hong Kong and Macau.
plaintiff.occupation_after: Salesman (employed by Yeung Wai Kwong from about 1st October, 2001); part-time driver from May 2000 to January 2001.

injuries.description: Diffuse axonal brain injury / severe head injury
source: Radiological examination showed diffuse brain injury but no skull fracture.
Urgent CT brain and cervical spine showed diffuse axonal brain injury with few spots of petechial haemorrhage. Cervical spine was normal.
Permanent Disability: best settled in Medical Assessment Board.
injuries.icd_description: Diffuse injury of multiple parts of brain

source: postconcussional disorder which was an acquired impairment in cognitive functioning, accompanied by specific neurobehavioural symptoms, that occurs as a consequence of closed head injury of sufficient severity to produce a significant cerebral concussion.

He finally opined that the plaintiff had great difficulty in returning to work as a salesman because of the impairment to his intellectual and mental function, slow response, lack of confidence in meeting people, difficulty in expressing his ideas and his speech was not fluent.

manifestations.description: memory loss / mild impairment of memory
occasional headache (episodes lasting several hours or around half an hour depending on report)
reduced confidence, anxiety in crowded places and social avoidance
difficulty in expressing ideas / impaired comprehension at times / slower thinking and response
clumsiness of left upper and lower limbs (reported earlier, improved later)

treatments_received: Intensive Care Unit admission with intracranial pressure catheter monitoring
Transfer to general ward and convalescent rehabilitation at Cheshire Home
Physiotherapy (30 treatments at PWH Physiotherapy Department)
Occupational therapy (27 treatments at PWH Occupational Therapy Department)
Speech therapy at PWH for 1 year
Acupuncture and Chinese physiotherapy (9 March 1999 to 10 May 1999)
treatments_future: Some short-term psychiatric treatment (accepted by the Court on Dr. Ho's evidence)

losses.description: Subtle and patchy cognitive impairment, mild impairment of intellectual and memory function, slower thinking and response, difficulty in organizing thought and expressing ideas.

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: Did not want to go to crowded places, felt people gave him a strange look, felt anxious when people looked at him.
Restricted social life, became less sociable, lost his girl friend.
Some change in character; became less sociable and ill tempered (as noted in evidence).

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Could not engage in mahjong, snooker and mind-using games that were leisure activities prior to the accident; could only listen to music and watch films and videos.
Unable to resume pre-accident role as a sales manager; can perform the job of a salesman but would not be a wholly fit salesman.

comparable_cases.injury_description: Severe head injuries including cerebral concussion, cerebral contusion, brain stem contusion, a fracture of the base of the skull compound into the left ear, facial bruising including the eyelids.

comparable_cases.case_name: Tse Ngan Heung v. Lo Sin Tak and Another HCPI No. 565 of 1999

comparable_cases.case_name: Yuen Yee Tak v. Hung Sang Engineering Works Ltd. HCA No. 8495 of 1985
comparable_cases.injury_description: Multiple injuries including depressed fracture over parietal and left region of the head and frontal epidural haematoma; left limb spastic and dyspraxia; mental capacity impaired.
